integration_preconditions: Trusted launcher creates Runtime from the existing exact Registry session, matching Authorizer and boot nonce. Runtime requires authorized root enumeration and validates workspace/root/task/policy before and after live work. I14 is trusted event ingress only and cannot grant read/write authority.

Use caller-supplied shared budgets: control Budget reserves sizeof(Runtime) and one Linux watcher FD; Options.work_budget reserves actual traversal allocation bounds plus depth+4 FDs and one CPU permit, or three temporary FDs and one CPU permit for recursive watch refresh. Do not construct independent per-request budget caps.

Call start before the initial reconcile. Call poll/reconcile from the workspace actor; the operation gate returns Busy for overlapping/reentrant work. Native callbacks only call invalidate and copy bounded paths. Index invalidation and snapshots support concurrent callbacks; source I/O and cache/registry calls stay outside its mutex.

Stop new calls and join every Runtime and Index/callback borrower before exclusive Runtime.deinit. Busy is not a concurrent destruction barrier. Registry, Authorizer, budgets, trusted-exclude handles and cache outlive their uses. Native macOS start/poll/refresh/stop must stay on the same native thread with stable Runtime address.

LiveResult.coverage.scope and reasons borrow Runtime-owned storage until its next live walk/reconcile or deinit. Copy before admitting another operation. Traversal sink paths are borrowed only during push. Caller sink/request storage outlives synchronous traversal.

checked_live files and search use enumerateLive/searchCandidatesLive (or the existing authoritative T05 traversal) even when index state is live. Never use watcher state as an atomic snapshot, content hash, immutable cache authorization, or complete candidate oracle.

Options.content_cache optionally connects T13: actor-side invalidation detaches mutable workspace associations while live pins retain immutable storage. Do not evict pinned content in an event callback.
Trusted exclude handles follow the existing T05 host binding contract: replacement requires host revalidation/rebinding. Watch streams do not turn old external exclude handles into current policy.

Linux needs public inotify and procfs /proc/self/fd to bind each watch to a verified no-follow directory handle. Backend failure, unavailable support, incomplete coverage, cancellation or dropped events preserves uncertain/live fallback; safe read/search remains usable.
limitations: Native macOS SDK linking, stream delivery/teardown, resource measurement and Windows runtime are NOT_RUN. Native Linux x86_64 only is runtime-proven.

Darwin public FSEvents adapter uses a private same-thread CFRunLoop mode. Scheduling API is deprecated but public. Without a native-proven delivery barrier synchronized stays false, so Darwin never falsely publishes a clean index.

Linux native registration is bounded at128 active slots. Incomplete registration, unusual filesystem behavior, dropped events and churn recovery keep uncertainty explicit; retired slots are reused conservatively.

Reconciliation performs a full-root covering rescan for all coalesced paths, uses the current T05 10,000-result cap and default max_depth32, and has at most3 passes (hard8). Truncation, coverage skips or ongoing events leave uncertain state with unchanged published index generation.
Only checked_live candidate traversal is implemented; bounded_stale/managed-generation cached candidate paths are not provided. No performance threshold or atomic snapshot is claimed.

Linux kernel watch memory and Darwin framework-internal allocations are not represented as Zig heap measurements. Explicit Zig control allocations, CPU/FD reservations and registration/batch counts are bounded; actual macOS resource accounting remains a release gate.
